newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt slips with U.S. Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt slips with U.S. Treasuries.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were lower with U.S. Treasuries amid concerns over a strong economy and nervousness about a possible tightening by the Federal Reserve, emerging market debt sources said.
"Our market is down with U.S. Treasuries on concerns of a Fed tightening," said one emerging markets trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
They said concerns mounted after a major U.S. investment bank said the Fed would adopt a more restrictive monetary policy after the first quarter of 1997.
"One forecast saying that it would raise Fed Funds by 25 basis points after each quarter bringing the funds rate up to 6 percent spooked the market," one market source said.
James O'SUllivan, economist at J.P. Morgan told Reuters there was no change in its forecasts and that its forecast for a tightening of 75 basis points was nothing new.
"We didn't change anything," he said, adding that there is "nothing new about it."
Nonetheless, Brady bond prices, along with other financial markets fell on the concerns.
Market experts also said trading activity thinned ahead of the U.S. producer prices due out Thursday and the U.S. employment report due out Friday.
One source noted, however, that the Brady bond yield spreads against U.S. Treasuries were virtually unchanged despite the drop in prices.
The biggest loser on the day were Russian Vneshkonombank loans, which fell sharply on news that Russian President Boris Yeltsin was taken to the hospital with signs that he may have pneumonia.
"News that Yeltsin was ordered back into the hospital pushed Vnesh prices lower," another source said.
Russian dollar-denominated Vnesh loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 1-1/2 weaker at 78 bid and the mark loans RUVNDMLNS=RR were 7/8 lower at 83-1/2 bid.
Elsewhere, Bulgaria's Brady bonds erased most of the gains scored Tuesday on news that the country would meet a $135.5 million coupon payment on its Brady bonds due January 28.
Bulgaria's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 5/8 softer at 50-7/8 bid and the country's FLRBs BGFLIRB=RR were 5/8 lower at 37-1/8.
In the broader market, Argentine pars were off 5/8 at 61-3/8, Brazil's "C" bonds were down 1/4 at 74 bid and Mexico's UMS-26 MXUMS=RR were off 1/4 at 105-1/4 bid.
